plans.note: Section 21 has a mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a consequential-damages exclusion with direct-damage clarifications, and an Excluded Claims definition covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnity, gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud and IP infringement. Check mutuality and whether the carve-out set is complete; 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit liability.

No indemnity section appears in the outline: Section 20 is missing though 9.3 cross-references 'Section 20.5' (IP infringement remedies) and 21.3 refers to 'indemnification obligations'. Verify whether Section 20 exists in the full text; if truly absent, treat the Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity as missing despite the dangling cross-references.

Section 12.4 (second instance) bars Customer from developing, marketing, selling or acquiring any competing product or service for the term plus 24 months in any territory — a direct restraint on our business and a walk-away item. Note the conflict with 12.3, which states Customer has made no non-compete commitment.

Section 7.2 (first instance) requires Customer to disclose and match any better third-party offer before engaging another provider, which operates as a de facto exclusivity/right-of-first-refusal; 12.3 disclaims exclusivity and 2.1 imposes take-or-pay volume, both relevant context.

The disclose-and-match duty in Section 7.2 (first instance) is an MFN running against us — it obliges Customer to surrender competitive pricing information for Vendor's benefit. Coordinate with the EXCLUSIVITY analysis so the same term is not double-flagged unless both rules are independently breached.

Section 12.4 (first instance) is a one-way 24-month bar on soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee 'regardless of how the employee applies' — no general-advertising carve-out and not limited to personnel involved in the Services; 12.3 conflicts by preserving general-recruitment hiring.

Section 9 offers only for-cause, insolvency and security/service-level termination (9.1–9.3, 9.5) plus force-majeure exit in 27.3; there is no Section 9.4 or other convenience right for Customer, and 2.1 expressly denies termination rights. Confirm no convenience clause sits in Section 9.4 or the Order Form provisions before marking missing.

Section 8.2 gives 30-day non-renewal notice with a 60-day Vendor reminder and deadline extension if not sent; 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice. Likely compliant — assess against preferred notice window and uplift cap.

Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction — outside the accepted list — while 28.2 gives exclusive jurisdiction to New York County courts, creating a direct conflict; 28.3 adds a pre-suit executive escalation that preserves urgent relief.

Section 24.1 permits Customer assignment to Affiliates/successors without consent, 24.2 restricts Vendor assignment and change of control, and 24.4 bars Vendor from terminating or repricing on our change of control; 13.3 allows transfer of licence rights. Likely compliant or better.

Section 14.1 confirms Customer ownership of Customer Data and pre-existing IP, but 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for Customer with only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence — contrary to owning what we pay for. Read with 13.2's perpetual paid-up licence and 14.3's Vendor Technology carve-back, which conflict with 14.2.

Sections 13.1–13.3 grant a worldwide licence extending to Affiliates and contractors, a perpetual paid-up licence for delivered Vendor Technology, and limit revocation/suspension to uncured material breach after notice. Tension with 14.2's revocable Deliverable licence should be noted, primarily under IP.

Section 22 limits Vendor audits to once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable, independent auditor, Vendor bears cost unless a >5% underpayment is found, with data-access protections. Likely compliant.

No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee payable by Customer appears; the take-or-pay in 2.1 is the closest economic penalty but belongs under MINCOMMIT. Note the absence of service credits in our favour (service-level exhibit referenced in 2.2 but not in this outline).

Section 19 provides professional-services, conformity (90 days for Deliverables, full subscription term for hosted Services), malicious-code and compliance warranties, with repair/re-perform then terminate-and-refund in 19.4 and a non-exclusive-remedy statement; 19.5 preserves express warranties. Likely compliant.

Section 18.1 sets CGL, workers' comp, employer's liability, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M for the term plus one year; 18.2 covers certificates, primacy and no limitation of liability. Check limits against playbook thresholds given health data exposure.

Section 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights — squarely against the no-take-or-pay-without-exit position, and inconsistent with 12.3's disclaimer of minimum-volume commitments and the absence of any convenience exit.

Section 10.1 references an 'agreed transition period' and 10.2 requires delivery of Deliverables and refunds, but no express obligation to provide transition/migration assistance or to return or export Customer Data in a usable format is visible (Section 11, cross-referenced in 16.5, is not in the outline). Verify Section 11 before concluding; otherwise the data-return and exit-assistance mechanics are missing.
